einzeiler: Former Navy SEAL commander Mike Hayes on combat, White House crisis management, and…
kurzfassung: Mike Hayes shares his journey from BUDS and deployments in South America, Kosovo, and Iraq to serving in the White House during the Captain Phillips rescue. He reflects on the heavy toll of war, the importance of keeping teams mission-ready, and transitioning to corporate leadership. The conversation also highlights his philanthropic foundation paying off Gold Star family mortgages and his involvement with the Medal of Honor Museum.
stichpunkte: Survived being held at gunpoint in Peru early in his career
Served at the White House under Presidents Bush and Obama, managing START treaty negotiations and the Captain Phillips rescue
Commanded SEAL Team 2 in Afghanistan through intense combat and high casualty rates
Established the 1162 Foundation, which donates all book profits to pay off mortgages for Gold Star widows
Transitioned to corporate leadership roles at Bridgewater, VMware, and Insight Partners
Helped launch the National Medal of Honor Museum in Arlington, Texas
Emphasizes the value of systematic decision-making, rigorous debriefs, and proactive mental health checks among veterans

clips.hook: A life-or-death choice during a kidnapping in Peru
clips.text: The speaker recalls a moment while being driven around by armed men in South America when he contemplated jumping from the vehicle to escape, but realized he could not abandon his comrade.

clips.hook: Negotiating nuclear treaties with foreign delegates at age 35
clips.text: The speaker describes sitting across the negotiating table from Russian representatives in Moscow while leading a high-level diplomatic delegation for the United States.

clips.hook: Starting over financially after decades of military service
clips.text: After spending twenty years in elite military units, the speaker reflects on leaving the service with minimal savings and facing the daunting reality of building a civilian career from scratch.

clips.hook: Preserving the legacy of America's greatest heroes
clips.text: The speaker explains the core philosophy behind building a national institution dedicated to recipients of the nation's highest military decoration, focusing on honoring their character and values.

beschreibung:
Mike Hayes is a retired Navy SEAL commander, national security leader, and business executive. He spent 20 years in the SEALs, ultimately serving as commanding officer of SEAL Team TWO and leading a 2,000-person special operations task force in Afghanistan. He later served on the National Security Council for Presidents George W. Bush and Barack Obama where he worked on the START Treaty and led the White House response to the Maersk Alabama hijacking. Today, he is a Managing Director at Insight Partners and the bestselling author of Never Enough and Mission Driven. Hayes draws on his experience across combat, government, and business to speak on leadership, decision-making, and purpose.
